articles.title: Serbia will not impose Russia sanctions – election winner’s rep to RT
articles.body:
Serbia will not impose Russia sanctions – election winner’s rep to RT
Serbia will maintain its longstanding ties with Russia and will not impose sanctions on Moscow despite EU pressure, a representative of the winning Student List movement has told RT Balkan.
The student-led opposition secured 52.73% of the vote in Sunday’s parliamentary election, according to the latest preliminary results, defeating the coalition of former President Aleksandar Vucic. He conceded defeat but warned that Belgrade could abandon its resistance to EU pressure and sanction Russia within months.
The movement emerged from nearly two years of anti-government protests sparked by the November 2024 collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad, which killed 16 people.
Speaking on Monday, Jovo Bakic, a university professor and Student List representative, said: “We respect Russia both as a great power and as our historically important partner and, in many cases, protector.”
“There will be no changes in that regard,” he added.
Recalling the harsh UN sanctions against Yugoslavia in the 1990s, when Serbia was one of its constituent republics, Bakic said restrictions imposed by “small Serbia” would have little effect on Russia but would be “symbolically very bad” for Belgrade.
🇷🇸 Jovo Bakić za RT Balkan: Studentska lista neće uvoditi sankcije Rusiji ▪️Predstavnik "Studentske liste", profesor Jovo Bakić ponovio je da nova vlada Srbije neće uvoditi sankcije Rusiji, uprkos tvrdnjama bivšeg predsednika Aleksandra Vučića da će se to dogoditi za nekoliko meseci. "Mi Rusiju poštujemo i kao veliku silu i kao našu istorijski važnu partnerku i u mnogim slučajevima zaštitnicu. Tu (u spoljnoj politici zemlje) neće biti nikakvih promena", izjavio je Bakić gostujući u emisiji "Srbija bira" na TV RT Balkan.
— RT Balkan (@rtbalkan) October 26, 2026
Under Vucic, Serbia resisted EU demands to adopt the bloc’s restrictions on Russia over the Ukraine conflict, despite pursuing EU membership. The Student List campaigned primarily on domestic reforms, leaving several contentious foreign policy questions unaddressed.
According to Reuters, leading candidates of the victorious movement have said the incoming government would halt arms exports to conflict zones, including sales to Western intermediaries that subsequently supply weapons to Ukraine.
Vucic previously said European buyers could decide how to use Serbian ammunition, including whether to send it to Ukraine, although Belgrade has denied supplying Kiev directly.
Energy ties present another major issue for Serbia’s incoming government. Russia remains the country’s dominant gas supplier, accounting for roughly three-quarters of its needs. In March, Vucic said Russian President Vladimir Putin had agreed to maintain deliveries on favorable terms, at prices far below those in most of Europe. The agreement was subsequently prolonged through the end of 2026.
Serbia also faces uncertainty over its oil supplies due to US sanctions on NIS, the majority Russian-owned energy company that runs the country’s only oil refinery. Hungarian energy group MOL is seeking to acquire the Russian stake, while the current US waiver allowing NIS to continue business expires on October 30. The company has requested another extension to avoid disruptions to fuel supplies.
Unlike Serbia, the EU has sought to phase out Russian fossil fuel imports and secure alternative suppliers since the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in 2022.
Asked about pressure to abandon Russian energy supplies, Bakic said: “We are not here to satisfy foreigners, but to act in our national interest.”
The Kremlin said on Monday that it hoped to maintain mutually beneficial relations with Serbia. Spokesman Dmitry Peskov praised Vucic’s contribution to bilateral ties and added “As you know, it takes two to tango.”

articles.title: Iran and “Mecca Pact” countries agree to continue talks amid fears of renewed regional conflict
articles.body:
Iran and representatives of Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey have agreed to continue diplomatic discussions following an initial meeting in Tehran, amid growing concerns over a renewed escalation of conflict in the Middle East.
The talks brought together officials from the three countries that signed the “Mecca Pact” joint defence agreement, as regional tensions intensify following renewed hostilities involving Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi movement.
Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman traveled to Tehran for the meeting, alongside Pakistan’s Army Chief Asim Munir, Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin and other senior officials.
According to a statement from the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the delegation’s visit was intended to “de-escalate the current crisis and promote dialogue and diplomatic solutions.”
Iranian state television reported Monday that the participants had agreed to continue discussions aimed at strengthening cooperation, including in the areas of regional peace and security.
The meeting took place amid warnings from the United States and Israel concerning the possibility of renewed military hostilities in the region.
It marked the first joint visit to Tehran by senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey since the three countries established their defence alliance last August.
READ: Mecca Defense Alliance agrees to ‘immediately’ implement collective defense commitments
The diplomatic initiative comes against the backdrop of renewed confrontations between Saudi Arabia and the Iranian-backed Houthi movement, which resumed in July following the collapse of a truce that had been in place in Yemen since 2022.
Riyadh supports Yemen’s internationally recognized government, while the Houthis remain a major force in the country’s prolonged conflict.
The talks also coincided with the Egyptian parliament’s approval of defence support for Saudi Arabia in response to Houthi attacks originating from Yemen.
Regional tensions have intensified ahead of Israel’s parliamentary elections scheduled for Tuesday, 27th October, and the US midterm elections the following week, in which President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is seeking to retain control of both chambers of Congress.
As the discussions began in Tehran on Monday, UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for urgent efforts to prevent further regional escalation.
“It is urgent to put an end to any escalation,” Guterres said, emphasizing the need to contain tensions as diplomatic efforts continue.
The agreement to maintain discussions signals a continued diplomatic effort by Iran and the three countries to address regional security concerns, although no specific commitments or outcomes beyond further talks were announced.
READ: Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia agree to continue regional security cooperation

articles.title: Air Force Spokesperson: Russian forces launch several ballistic missile strikes on Pivdenny Bridge in Kyiv
articles.body:
During the latest attack, Russian forces launched several ballistic missile strikes against the Southern Bridge (Pivdenny) in Kyiv. While such structures are not easily destroyed, repairing the damaged bridge deck will take time, Yuriy Ihnat, a spokesperson for the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, stated during a televised marathon on Tuesday.
"Of course, the bridge deck can be repaired—bridges are not as easy to destroy as some might think. Nevertheless, this does cause certain inconveniences, and repairs will take time," Ihnat said.
According to him, the adversary employed 16 ballistic missiles—either Iskander-M missiles or S-400 surface-to-air guided missiles—during the recent attack. Specialists examining the impact site will determine the exact type of missiles used. "The adversary used two types of missiles today: either Iskander-M or S-400 surface-to-air missiles," the spokesperson noted.
Ihnat emphasized that over the past two weeks, Russian forces have focused their missile strikes on Kyiv, launching ballistic missiles in several waves throughout the night and combining them with drone attacks.
"Previously, ballistic missile strikes might have occurred just once a night. Now, they are spread out over several waves of attacks... They launch these strikes in waves, and all of this is accompanied by drone attacks," he said.
As previously reported, Taras Chmut, head of the Come Back Alive foundation and a military analyst, stated in an interview with DW that the complete destruction of bridges in Kyiv by Russian shelling is a possibility, provided the adversary is willing to commit significant resources. At the same time, he noted that destroying a single section of a bridge does not necessarily lead to the collapse of the entire structure; the critical issue remains how quickly a crossing can be restored, at least in some capacity. According to him, even partial damage to bridges could severely complicate urban logistics, particularly the operation of the metro system and public transport.
"I wouldn't rule out such a scenario; if the Russians are determined enough and willing to expend the necessary resources, they could certainly do it," he emphasized.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported that on Tuesday, the enemy struck the Pivdenny Bridge in Kyiv, damaging metro infrastructure located on the span.
Kyiv Metro has temporarily suspended service between Osokorky and Chervony Khutir stations on the green line due to the damage to infrastructure on the Pivdenny Bridge. Furthermore, with the Pivdenny Bridge closed, both freight and passenger vehicle traffic have been diverted along alternative routes.

articles.title: Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia agree to continue regional security cooperation
articles.body:
Iran, Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia have agreed to continue dialogue to strengthen cooperation on regional peace and security, according to a joint statement issued after a four-way meeting in Tehran.
The statement said the four countries had agreed to continue dialogue to enhance cooperation, including in the fields of regional peace and security.
The first meeting of the four countries was held in the Iranian capital on Monday, 26 October 2026.
The meeting was hosted by Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council.
Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin also attended.
READ: Pakistan can mediate between Washington and Tehran, but it cannot manufacture trust
Participants agreed to continue talks to strengthen cooperation among the four countries.
Iranian state television announced the start of the meeting on Monday, saying it was dedicated to discussing regional security and stability.
Iran’s Foreign Ministry also said Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi attended a meeting between President Masoud Pezeshkian and representatives responsible for defence and security affairs from Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.
Meanwhile, Reuters quoted a senior Iranian official as saying that Tehran’s talks with members of the “Mecca Alliance” did not cover Iran’s nuclear programme.
The official added that Iran would not discuss its nuclear programme until the United States responded to its demands for ending the war.

articles.title: Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv kills one and injures 10, damaging medical facilities and student accommodation – photos
articles.body:
Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv kills one and injures 10, damaging medical facilities and student accommodation – photos
Russia attacked the city of Kyiv with ballistic missiles on the evening of 26 October. One person has been killed and 10 injured, including students living in a hall of residence.
Source: Ukraine's Air Force; monitoring Telegram channels; Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko
Details: At 21:41, the Air Force warned of a ballistic missile threat from the Russian city of Bryansk.
Several subsequent reports said missiles were heading towards Kyiv from Chernihiv Oblast.
Explosions were heard in Kyiv a few minutes later.
Klitschko said a strike had been recorded near one of the metro stations in the Desnianskyi district.
Update: Klitschko later reported that a medical facility in the Dniprovskyi district had been damaged in the attack.
The blast wave shattered windows in the intensive care unit.
Windows were also shattered in two departments at another medical facility in the same district.
No patients or medical staff were injured.
A building in a non-residential area of the Dniprovskyi district was also hit. Early reports indicated that one person had been killed near a nearby supermarket.
Klitschko added that two emergency medical workers who had arrived at the scene were among those injured: a paramedic and an emergency medical technician. Their injuries were not believed to be critical.
A strike was recorded near a residential building in the Desnianskyi district. People may have been trapped inside, according to early reports.
As of 22:41, five people had been injured in the capital.
The number of people injured later rose to seven.
Kyiv City Military Administration reported that student accommodation belonging to an educational institution had been damaged in the Desnianskyi district.
Klitschko wrote that a 20-year-old woman had been injured near the building.
As of 23:24, one person is known to have been killed and 10 injured in the attack. Most of those injured are students from a university hall of residence.

articles.title: Anduril unveils family of air defence interceptors
articles.body:
Anduril has revealed Steelfin, a family of surface-to-air interceptor missiles built on a common two-stage architecture so that one production line can turn out versions for everything from point defence to upper-tier ballistic missile defence, according to the company.
The company set out the problem it is addressing, saying adversaries have invested in large volumes of low-cost, mass-producible offensive weapons and that air defence batteries are too often forced to expend exquisite interceptors against lower-cost threats, straining stores of the most critical defensive weapons and putting defenders on the losing side of the cost exchange.
Steelfin pairs a first-stage booster, which can take different solid rocket motors to suit range, launch configuration or packing density, with a second-stage terminal interceptor sharing the same airframe, avionics, software, flight control system and interfaces across every variant. Open interfaces between the subsystems in that terminal stage let different seekers and mission systems be fitted without redesigning the missile.
Because the variants share an architecture and components, they move through the same production line using the same tooling, technicians and facilities, and Anduril said it is planning to produce on the order of several thousand Steelfin variants a year in the short term, with capacity designed to flex to demand. The same open interfaces allow commercial off-the-shelf components and competition between vendors, widening the supplier base.
The missiles are compatible with launch infrastructure already in service, including the M903A2 launcher used by Patriot, the Mk 41 vertical launching system fitted to warships, Typhon and emerging containerised launchers, and are designed to integrate with fielded fire control systems such as Aegis and IBCS. Anduril has completed ballistic testing with representative air vehicles and will begin flight testing next year.
The American company has built a European presence over the past two years, with Latvia selecting its Barracuda cruise missile family and a United Kingdom arm working on autonomy, counter-drone systems and command software. Its approach of designing weapons around mass production and common components is the same argument being made by Helsing, which launched its own pair of low-cost interceptors this week.

articles.title: Ukrainian postal service forms private air defense force, shoots down Russian drones
articles.body:
Ukrainian postal service forms private air defense force, shoots down Russian drones
Ukrainian postal and courier company Nova Poshta has started its own private air defense force and shot down Russian attack drones targeting their facilities, Vyacheslav Klymov, co-owner of the Nova group of companies, revealed at the Kyiv International Economic Forum on Oct. 26.
"We are one of the few companies that has implemented this project. I don't want to disclose the numbers, but we have destroyed 'Shahed' drones," Klimov said.
Nova Poshta is the largest private postal and courier company in Ukraine, operating over 15,817 branches across the country, and employing over 34,000 people. Its post offices and distribution centers have frequently come under Russian attack.
Despite the ongoing war, business is going well for Nova Poshta. The company quadrupled its net profit compared with last year, according to financial reports published on April 27.
Klimov also emphasised the importance of companies having their own private firefighting capabilities, rather than just waiting for the response of state authorities.
Nova Poshta employees frequently put out significant fires on their premises before the arrival of state emergency service firefighters, Klimov said.
"Now big businesses are looking for fire engines in Europe in order to create their own services. This is our property… who can forbid me from putting out a fire on my own territory?" he said.
Since late summer, Russia has been attacking Ukraine with jet-powered drones, adding to the now-familiar threat posed by conventional Shahed-type drones and missiles. Between larger assaults, successive waves of jet-powered drones now arrive day and night.
Russia's jet-powered drones target civilian infrastructure such as supermarkets, schools, shopping malls, telecommunications infrastructure, data centers, gas stations, and medical facilities.

articles.title: AFRL Moves Cargo Through Space with SpaceX Demonstration
articles.body:
Editor’s Note: This story was updated Oct. 26 with additional information from the Air Force Research Laboratory.
When a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket took off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Fla., on Oct. 20, it didn’t only carry the usual mix of micro-satellites and cubesats built by a wide range of companies. Also catching a ride into orbit was a capsule containing, among other things, a reverse osmosis desalinator, survival gear, and emergency medical equipment.
That capsule wasn’t bound for the only humans in space on the International Space Station; it was a test of a capability that could one day get critical supplies to U.S. forces around the globe.
The Air Force Research Laboratory launched its Rocket Cargo initiative in 2021 to explore the idea of moving large amounts of cargo through space, a process that would both be faster and allow the Pentagon to more easily reach remote or contested areas.
SpaceX, which has demonstrated the ability to return its rockets to Earth and safely land them, was the first company to get a contract under the program in 2022, when AFRL awarded the firm a five-year, $102 million contract.
Other companies, including Blue Origin, Sierra Space, and Rocket Lab, have since signed on as well, but AFRL never announced any experiments or tests for the project—until now.
In a release, AFRL said the Oct. 20 mission “used a SpaceX capsule with instrumentation to measure temperature, shock and vibration; it carried agile cargo pod designs built for various delivery loads.”
The lab did not specify how many pods or how much equipment were included in the test and did not immediately respond to a query. But in a subsequent social media post Oct. 26, the lab said it recovered the pods after they splashed down in the Pacific Ocean. Each pod had equipment and sensors to monitor the payload’s status as it launched and then reentered the atmosphere.
“Researchers paid special attention to the electronics equipment, including a satellite communication-enabled tracker, batteries, a reverse osmosis desalinator, survival gear and emergency medical equipment,” the release states.
The SpaceX capsule used in the test is called Starfall. Back in May, the Federal Aviation Administration released an environmental assessment for Starfall operations in the Pacific Ocean, describing it as a “cylindrical shaped capsule” with these dimensions:
- Approximately 0.75 meters (2.5 feet) tall
- A diameter of 3.1 meters (10.2 feet)
- A weight of 2,100 kilograms (4,600 pounds)
- Capable of carrying 1,000 kilograms (2,200 pounds) of payload
- Total weight of 3,100 kilograms (6,800 pounds)
In June, SpaceX launched what it called a “Starfall Demo Mission,” ending with the capsule splashing down into the Pacific.
In a statement, AFRL’s Technology Transition Office director Adam Remaly touted the most recent test as a success.
“This was a critical achievement to demonstrate the potential of Rocket Cargo delivery for point-to-point rapid global mobility for the future force,” Remaly said. “The cross-discipline collaborations and ability to unleash the speed of our defense industrial base are key to maximizing capability and winning the future.”
AFRL’s release noted that engineers also “measured the capsule to potentially include a life raft in future tests” on Oct. 20.
Rocket Cargo could one day deliver supplies “to contested environments and austere sites without access to runways and roads, including contested logistics, expeditionary operations, rescue operations, disaster relief and response to chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear hazards,” the release states.

articles.title: 30 Kilometers With a Wounded Soldier: CODE 9.2 Conducted Two Air Evacuations Using the StarGate Drone
articles.body:
Over the course of a week, the CODE 9.2 regiment carried out two air evacuations of the wounded from the battlefield using the StarGate drone — these are the second and third known instances of such an evacuation in the world.
The regiment told Militarnyi that ground transport could not reach the positions where the wounded were located.
They evacuated 25-year-old Yevhen, call sign Izium, and 24-year-old Artem, call sign Kolobok.
Both soldiers had suffered severe injuries to their limbs and were stationed in the gray zone, approximately five kilometers from the state border with Russia.
Air evacuation remained the only available way to transport them to medical personnel.
The SkyFall team — the developer and manufacturer of StarGate drones — also joined in preparing for the operation.
Once the operation began, heavy Vampire strike drones were used to engage enemy positions.
During one of the missions, the StarGate drone traveled nearly 30 km one way to the soldier’s position and the same distance back, this time with the wounded soldier on board.
In the area of operations, the enemy actively employed electronic warfare measures in an attempt to completely jam the GPS signal.
Despite this, thanks to its onboard AI-based navigation system and the pilots’ skill, the drone was able to continue flying without satellite navigation and successfully complete the evacuation mission.
“Going forward, we plan to make changes to our regiment’s organizational structure and establish a separate medical aviation unit within the medical company. It will specialize specifically in evacuating the wounded from the battlefield by air,” emphasized Regiment Commander Oleksandr Nastenko, call sign Flint.
Previously, soldiers from the 92nd Separate Mechanized Brigade and the 30th Separate Mechanized Brigade for the first time evacuated a wounded soldier using a hexacopter.
StarGate is Ukraine’s first specialized unmanned aerial platform for evacuating the wounded from the battlefield (CASEVAC), developed by the technology and defense company SkyFall.
It was created at the request of the military for situations where ground transport cannot reach the wounded or where its use is too dangerous.
The drone can carry up to 150 kg of payload and reach speeds of up to 105 km/h.
The evacuation module is based on certified medical stretchers.
Onboard artificial intelligence, navigation, and redundant communication systems allow the mission to continue even if the GPS signal is jammed or communication is lost.

articles.title: Putin holds call with leaders of Norway, Finland – Kremlin
articles.body:
Putin holds call with leaders of Norway, Finland – Kremlin
Russian President Vladimir Putin has held a phone call with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, discussing efforts to resolve the Ukraine conflict, the Kremlin announced on Tuesday.
The conversation was initiated by the Finnish and Norwegian sides and followed last week’s meetings involving US special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg, and the Oslo discussions between Stubb, Store, and Vladimir Zelensky.
The Kremlin said the Nordic leaders welcomed the agreement to resume trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the US in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November. The negotiations will address security arrangements for Russia and Ukraine after the conflict ends, among other issues.
During the phone call, Putin emphasized the root causes of the Ukraine conflict, stating that a just and lasting peace requires Russia’s legitimate interests to be fully and unconditionally taken into account.
He also criticized the confrontational policies of EU and NATO countries, saying they are prolonging the fighting.
The three leaders also discussed security and stability in the Baltic Sea and Northern Europe. According to the Kremlin, Stubb and Store reaffirmed the importance of upholding international maritime law and the principle of freedom of navigation.
Putin also informed his Nordic counterparts of the start of a US-mediated humanitarian operation near Alyoshki in Kherson Region, Russia, with a temporary ceasefire introduced in the area.
The conversation ended with a mutual agreement to maintain direct telephone contact, the Kremlin said.
The call was a rare direct exchange between Putin and European leaders, most of whom have shunned contact with Moscow since the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in 2022.
Stubb described Tuesday’s phone call with Putin as “frank and substantive,” stressing the importance of direct discussions. “We are neighboring countries to Russia. The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security.”
The two Nordic leaders said they took part in the call as leaders of their countries and were not speaking on behalf of Europe. They added that the call was held in consultation with Ukraine to convey its position ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks, and vowed to continue to support Kiev.

articles.title: European defense ministers warn Putin isn’t looking for peace
articles.body:
PARIS — Top European defense ministers and EU representatives said Ukraine faces challenging months ahead, insisting they must keep supporting Kyiv despite the U.S. bid for talks with Russia.
"The new diplomatic push is there, but it's also clear that Putin's actions tell a different story," the EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said at a press conference in Paris on Monday. Kallas said she was expecting a "brutal winter" for Kyiv and that there was "no hope for imminent peace," reiterating the need to help Ukraine "withstand the attacks and increase the cost for Russia."
Kallas, along with European Commissioner for Defence and Space Andrius Kubilius, joined a meeting with defense ministers from the E5 group made up of France, the U.K., Germany, Poland and Italy, hosted at the French armed forces ministry.
Advertisement
The meeting came amid a renewed U.S. effort to push Ukraine into peace talks with Russia and growing doubts about Washington's support for Kyiv.
U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff said last week he would offer Russia's Vladimir Putin direct talks with President Donald Trump and Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy to secure a ceasefire.
"No results whatsoever comes for those who want to negotiate with Putin," German defense minister Boris Pistoripus said. "The results are what? It doesn't lead to anything. There is no signal whatsoever that Putin is looking for peace."
The U.K.'s Wes Streeting added: "While none of us seek confrontation with Russia ... We do have to be aware of the threat posed by Russia."
While pledging "total transparency" with the U.S., France's Catherine Vautrin said the E5 members would "work together concretely," focusing on arms production and interoperability.
"Produce more, produce faster, produce equipment suited to today’s conflicts – but we must already be planning for the conflicts of tomorrow," Vautrin said. "On that, EU financial initiatives can help us move in this direction."

articles.title: At least 20 killed in airstrikes on Sudan’s South Darfur: Report
articles.body:
Sahin Demir
27 October 2026•Update: 27 October 2026
At least 20 people, including members of the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), were killed and dozens injured in airstrikes on the city of Nyala in Sudan’s South Darfur state, local media reported Tuesday.
The strikes hit several locations across the city late Monday, including a crowded night market and positions belonging to the RSF, Sudan Tribune reported, citing local sources and eyewitnesses.
A local source said at least 20 people were killed and dozens injured when airstrikes targeted two locations in Nyala.
One of the strikes hit the Tanguj Station night market in the Domaya area, where civilians and RSF recruits were reportedly present, resulting in heavy casualties.
Videos circulated by pro-RSF activists on social media purportedly showed bodies of RSF fighters killed in a drone strike on a gathering in Domaya.
Eyewitnesses said other strikes targeted the headquarters of the 16th Infantry Division, nearby positions and houses believed to belong to RSF commanders in the Al-Nahda, Al-Riyadh and Airport neighborhoods.
The attacks also reportedly hit a student housing complex belonging to Nyala University.
According to the report, the Sudanese army has intensified its air operations in Nyala over the past week, targeting RSF military positions, command facilities and air defense systems near Nyala International Airport.
Military sources said the operations were aimed at weakening the RSF’s defensive and offensive capabilities ahead of a possible ground offensive in Darfur and Kordofan.
There was no immediate comment from the Sudanese army or the RSF on the latest strikes.
Sudan has been engulfed in a conflict between the army and the RSF since April 2023, leaving tens of thousands dead and millions displaced.
The fighting has triggered one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises, with widespread food insecurity and famine reported in several parts of the country.

articles.title: The Trump administration is backing Orbán, who blocked a €90 billion EU loan to Ukraine, for UN secretary-general and is counting on support from Moscow and Beijing, WSJ says
articles.body:
The Trump administration has encouraged former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán to run for UN secretary-general and discussed a joint US-Russia-China candidacy with Moscow and Beijing, the Wall Street Journal’s (WSJ) editorial board wrote on 25 October, citing sources in three countries. Russia’s biggest ally in the EU, Orbán has been out of office since May, when Péter Magyar became Hungary’s prime minister.
The UN secretary-general can influence the war through diplomatic negotiations, mediation, and by drawing the Security Council’s attention to Russia’s aggression. António Guterres’s term ends on 31 December, so the council has to settle on a successor within weeks.
According to the WSJ, US officials discussing the next UN chief kept saying they wanted “someone like Orbán,” and their Russian and Chinese counterparts agreed. The US then brought the idea to Orbán himself. Russia and China are believed to support his bid based on those earlier talks with Washington, and the plan is for him to be the three countries’ joint candidate.
Ukraine warns of Orbán’s veto tactics at the UN
Orbán is receptive but has not decided, and he does not want to enter the race unless he is sure he can win, the editorial board wrote. A State Department official counted eight Security Council votes as safe for him and 10 within reach. A candidate needs nine of the 15 votes and no veto from a permanent member. The editorial board asked whether Britain and France, typically cautious in using their veto, would stand in the way. Any announcement is being held until after the 3 November US midterm elections.
Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha wrote on X that Orbán as secretary-general would put to good use “the masterful veto and blackmail skills” he developed over years of derailing major EU decisions. Ukraine, he added, could share its “great experience of taking him out for coffee at the right moment,” a reference to the December 2023 EU summit, where Orbán left the room so the other leaders could open accession talks with Ukraine without his veto.
Orbán ran Hungary for 16 years as Putin’s closest EU partner
Orbán’s 16 years of “illiberal democracy” eroded democratic values in Hungary. Since 2010, Fidesz has built an enormous partisan media ecosystem. Before the vote, it amended the electoral law twice and gerrymandered more than a third of the electoral districts, so the opposition might need around 55% of the popular vote to win a simple majority. Orbán still lost the 12 April election. Magyar’s Tisza won 138 of 199 seats, a two-thirds majority in parliament.
Orbán kept close ties with Moscow throughout the full-scale war. When he met Putin in Beijing in October 2023, he spoke of “the military operations and the sanctions” rather than a war. In summer 2024, while Hungary held the EU Council presidency, he flew to Moscow on what he called a peace mission, and the EU distanced itself from the trip. In November 2025, he went back to Moscow, seeking to keep Hungary’s access to Russian oil and gas. He is widely considered Putin’s closest partner among EU leaders. After that visit, he said the only solution was for Ukraine to become a buffer state again, and that the longer peace was delayed, the more people and territory Ukraine would lose.
He used Hungary’s veto against Ukraine until his last weeks in office. In February, Orbán vetoed a €90 billion EU loan to Ukraine amid the disruption of Russian oil supplies through the Druzhba pipeline to Hungary and Slovakia. Hungary lifted its veto in April after repairs to the pipeline were announced. Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó phoned Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov from EU meetings for years with “live reports on what’s been discussed,” a European security official told The Washington Post. Szijjártó did not respond to the Post’s request for comment.

articles.title: American bomber escorted by British and Norwegian F-35s
articles.body:
British F-35Bs flying from HMS Prince of Wales and Norwegian F-35As have escorted a United States Air Force B-52 over the High North during Exercise Global Thunder, the American nuclear readiness exercise, according to a post by Defence Operations.
The post said: “UK F-35Bs & @RoyalAirForce Voyager, with @Luftforsvaret F-35As, escorted a @usairforce B-52 on Exercise Global Thunder. Above @RoyalNavy & @Forsvaret_no vessels including @HMSPWLS. Operating together to defend @NATO’s northern flank.”
An RAF Voyager tanker supported the formation. HMS Prince of Wales is in the Arctic and North Atlantic on the second phase of Operation Firecrest, accompanied by the Type 45 destroyer HMS Dauntless and operating under NATO command, a deployment this publication covered as the ship sailed.
United States Strategic Command describes Global Thunder as an annual exercise involving personnel throughout the strategic enterprise, including its own components and subordinate units, and says the purpose of Global Thunder 27 “is to enhance nuclear readiness and ensure a safe, secure, effective and credible strategic deterrent force.”
The command added: “This is an annual exercise and is not in response to actions by any nation, other actors or current world events,” and that “as in previous years, Global Thunder 27 may include an increase in bomber and other aircraft flights throughout the exercise.”
Britain’s part in the American nuclear exercise comes as the country prepares to take on a nuclear role of its own in the air again. The Defence Investment Plan confirmed the purchase of twelve F-35A aircraft and British entry into NATO’s nuclear mission, which will return a nuclear task to the Royal Air Force for the first time since the WE.177 bomb was withdrawn in 1998. RAF Typhoons also escorted French Rafales simulating a nuclear strike over the Mediterranean last week on Exercise Rummy, the first British participation in a French nuclear exercise.
Norway operates fifty two F-35As from Ørland and Evenes and has become one of the closest partners in British operations in the High North, hosting Royal Marines for Arctic training and working alongside the carrier group through the Firecrest deployment.

articles.title: Israel's mediacide in Gaza seeks to bury genocide evidence: UN
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
'Destruction of truth': UN report finds Israel's mediacide in Gaza seeks to bury evidence of genocide
Israel is attempting to "systematically eliminate" journalists in occupied Palestine in a bid to cover up evidence of genocide and war crimes, according to a UN report.
The paper, authored by UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese, says that "destruction of truth" has been integral to the assault on Gaza, and describes Israel's attempts to control information as "mediacide".
Israeli forces have killed hundreds of journalists in the occupied territories since October 2023 while most of Gaza's infrastructure lies in ruins.
“Genocide is never sustained by killing alone. It requires destroying the conditions in which killing can be seen, documented, remembered and judged,” Albanese said while presenting the report to the UN Human Rights Council on Monday.
The report identifies three ways in which Israel and its supporters attempt to destroy or hide evidence of crimes committed in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
These include the systematic targeting of journalists and communications infrastructure, and the Israeli government's attempts to censor and manipulate information.
It also highlights the complicity of Western news organisations and technology platforms, which it accuses of promoting Israeli narratives and suppressing Palestinian voices.
"These practices have not merely accompanied genocide but have facilitated its commission and obstructed accountability," the report reads.
The UN documented the killing of almost 300 Palestinian journalists between October 2023 and February this year. Hundreds of others have been wounded or unlawfully detained by Israeli authorities.
Some were killed in indiscriminate attacks while at least 70 are known to have been deliberately targeted.
Israel has replicated its assault on Palestinian journalists in its other conflicts in Lebanon, Yemen and Iran, where dozens of other media workers have been killed in airstrikes.
The report says that the Israeli military has wiped out more than 80% of Gaza's communications infrastructure and damaged another 12%. By October 2025, Israeli forces had destroyed 125 media offices and institutions, including news agency headquarters, broadcast towers and radio stations, it says.
Blackouts caused by the damage have prevented local journalists from broadcasting events and people outside the strip from verifying information.
The destruction has gone hand-in-hand with the Israeli government's media restrictions, which have prevented foreign journalists reporting from Gaza and censored thousands of articles related to the war.
"In the ongoing genocide, the systematic elimination of media witnesses and the destruction of the means of documentation are probative of genocidal intent," the report says.
"They reveal an effort not only to destroy a protected group, but also to destroy the conditions in which that destruction can be seen, documented, remembered and ultimately adjudicated," it continues.

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition thwarts wave of Houthi attacks on kingdom
articles.body:
The Saudi-led coalition against Houthis said Tuesday it intercepted wave of ballistic missiles and drones targeting two regions in Saudi Arabia, as the conflict with the Iran-aligned group intensifies.
The Houthis launched three ballistic missiles toward Saudi Arabia's Eastern Region and four drones toward the country's Southern Region, the coalition said.
Saudi Civil Defense issued early warnings for a potential threat in the Eastern Region and in Kharj governorate, later saying the danger had passed in both areas.
Saudi Arabia has intensified its strikes on the Houthis since the group captured strategic areas along Yemen's Red Sea coast last month, advancing toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key global shipping route for Gulf oil producers opposite the Strait of Hormuz on the Arabian Peninsula.
Earlier Monday, the coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three drones over the Riyadh region and southern Saudi Arabia, without identifying their origin or intended targets.
The coalition also announced strikes on Houthi positions in Yemen, saying it destroyed ballistic missile launchers, storage tunnels and a missile depot.
Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said the operations aimed to dismantle the group's ballistic missile network and disrupt its supply routes.
The renewed fighting between the two sides has shattered a 2022 U.N.-brokered truce that largely halted attacks between the Saudi-led coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognized government, and the Houthis, who control the capital Sanaa.
The escalation has also opened another front in regional conflicts involving the U.S., Israel and Iran.

articles.title: Zelensky accuses West of intentionally postponing Patriot, NASAMS missile deliveries
articles.body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Ukraine’s Vladimir Zelensky has accused Western partners of deliberately delaying deliveries of interceptor missiles for the country’s air defense systems in recent weeks.
Specifically, in a post on his Telegram channel, he described the delays in supplying interceptor missiles for the Patriot and NASAMS air defense systems as "artificial and prolonged."
Kiev had repeatedly complained about a shortage of interceptor missiles for its air defense. On October 15, CNN, citing sources, reported that Ukraine’s stockpile of Patriot missiles had been completely depleted. Later, Vladimir Zelensky voiced complaints about delays in the delivery of American interceptor missiles purchased with funding from European Union countries under the PURL (Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List) mechanism. He accused Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth of holding up the delivery of missiles for the Patriot and NASAMS air defense systems by a month.
